creator: Alexander Terp
description:
Running `./dev --ssh` and then `./dev --perf` reports a regression that is not one. The ssh tier leaves its devenv containers running, and `frame.decode` measures 1.67 ns/byte against a 0.83 baseline with them up and 1.44 with them stopped - so the obvious thing to do, running the out-of-gate tiers in sequence, produces a false failure.

Two things behind it. The containers are left running deliberately, since a devenv is a thing you keep; nothing says so at the point where it matters. And `frame.decode` now sits close enough to its 2.00x tolerance that ordinary machine load crosses it, which means the baseline was recorded on a quieter machine than the one anybody runs this on.

A perf tier that fails for reasons unrelated to the code is one people learn to skip, which costs more than the regression it was built to catch. Worth deciding between: measuring load and refusing to judge when the machine is busy, re-recording the baseline against a realistic machine, or having the ssh tier say what it left running.
title: 📉 The perf tier fails if you ran the ssh tier first
